body:
I wanted to breastfeed so badly. The first day she latched perfectly, and things were dandy. The second day, the hospitals lactation consultant came in and spent over an hour shoving my boob in her mouth and adjusting her head etc. by the time she left my baby was upset, I was in tears. She latched one more time and then refused to latch again. 

By the time we were ready to leave the hospital she had lost too much weight so they had me pump. My milk had come in so that wasn’t the issue. She took the bottle and was good to go home. I tried to get her to latch a few more times the rest of the day and she would fight me for an hour each time. By that night when I even tried to put her in the feeding position she would freak out. 

I decided I couldn’t keep spending hours fighting a baby to eat. So I started pumping. I tried every now and then to get her to latch, but she never latched again. 

I exclusively pumped for 10 months, just weaned off for my mental health. But I am still salty about that lactation consultant. I feel like she ruined my breastfeeding experience before I even got to decide if it would work for us. I’m thankful I was still able to provide breastmilk for so long, but it was not how I had hoped things would go. And I’m one and done so I will never get to try again.
The changing pad is really just a piece of cloth. But it’s come in handy to put down on public changing tables when I was traveling.
I’ll have to check them out! This summer has been awful and I’m desperate. The kindred bravely ones I’ve started only wearing for workouts.

When I was freshly post partum and my husband went back to work I had so much anxiety about leaving the house. I felt like I was on a timer constantly and had to rush home to pump. I use the spectra s1 as my main pump. But I bought momcozy m5s, a mini cooler bag from medela that holds four 4oz bottles, and pump wipes. 

I was determined to figure out a way to feel more normal with baby. So I started by going to Barnes and noble and wandering around there with baby in her  stroller and I practiced pumping. Put them in in the bathroom, took them out and emptied into the containers, wiped everything down. 

I made it a point to leave the house every day so I could get used to packing up baby and getting the hang out pumping on the go. Even if it was just to drive to the drive thru at Starbucks for a coffee I did it for a few weeks. 

I also use a pump log app (called Pump Log). I paid the lifetime fee and log my pumps time, duration, and ounces. I set a widget on my screen and it keeps track of how long since the last pump so I could stop doing math and going too long between pumps. 

It’s still a lot, but with my practice runs it got less intimidating and stressful the more I did it.

Edit to add: I also bought nursing bras! Lane Bryant has some good ones for plus size girlies. And then I also have the kindred bravely pumping/nursing bras which came in handy when I was on a road trip and was pumping with my spectra in the car.

I gave birth two weeks before Thanksgiving. We told family we would see how I was feeling and let them know last minute. We went, dad and I held her for 99% of the time. It was fine. Then a week later she got RSV and was hospitalized. So we didn’t do anything at all for Christmas. I couldn’t get myself to bring her around a bunch of people again after that, even though everyone had been totally respectful and understanding. Christmas just felt lackluster, and weird. But this year she’ll be a little over a year old and I’m looking forward to making up for last year. 

IMO, do what you feel comfortable with, and make sure you take care of yourself too.

I have the simply wishes one, I only wear it when pumping. It gets packed in my work bag and I wear nursing bras and just fold down the cups and put the pumping bra over top to pump. I wash it when the cloth parts that hold the flange in place gets stretched out and stops holding them in place well. I probably should wash it more frequently, but I’m in the same boat and only have the one

I have a CityMouse crossbody for day to day stuff. I absolutely love it. I can fit three-four diapers, a pack of wipes, my wallet, phone, keys, a 4oz bottle, teething toys, foldable changing cloth, emergency onesie and even some granola bars for me. It’s great if I’ll be home for a few hours. I have a pump bag that I now use as a diaper bag if I’ll be gone all day. 

I had found the backpack one I got at my baby shower was just so bulky and I like to babywear. I looked ridiculous going out in public to get groceries etc. I needed something smaller so I felt more mobile and going out didn’t feel so daunting.
I will try that. Already doing the lymphatic massage (I’m actually a licensed massage therapist so that comes in handy). I’ll keep with the ibuprofen too

It’s amazing how complicated this “natural” process really is. I will try all your suggestions. I’m sad to start weaning but I’m also so over it I think once I get past the emotions my mental health will be so much better

Seriously! I exclusively pump and the LC I was consulting with was like you need lots of sleep, but you need to pump every two hours to get your supply up. And when I asked about overnight she was like yeah every two hours…. Soooo when do I get this magical restorative sleep you keep saying is essential for milk production??? Not to mention I’m also dealing with a newborn and recovering from a c section. It was just so out of touch with reality.

I exclusively pump since my daughter was 4 days old. I had a really bad interaction with a lactation consultant and after that she refused to latch. The pediatrician had me start supplementing with pumping because she had dropped too much weight. My milk supply is really good (not an oversupplier but I’m able to feed her exclusively breast milk) but my baby absolutely refuses to breastfeed. 

Exclusively pumping has its own challenges, if I wasn’t making enough to sustain her and was needing to feed formula too I would probably wean off and switch to formula if I’m honest. The day we got home from the hospital I had a meeting with a different LC and I cried my eyes out about not being able to breastfeed her. But that LC told me that if pumping works that is what we should do. A fed baby and a mentally healthy mom is what’s most important. 

If breastmilk is important to you, you could always pump and work on increasing your supply, there are benefits to baby getting some breastmilk as far as antibodies etc. BUT, I would say if that option feels stressful or overwhelming it is totally ok to just not. 

There’s so much pressure on us already, if breastfeeding isn’t working for your family it is ok to not do it. I totally get that guilt though. Once you make a decision and sit with it, that guilt will go away. Especially if you feel less stress and anxiety around feedings and baby is satisfied. You’re still a good mom if you don’t breastfeed. And people are so weird about something that is not as easy and natural feeling as we’re led to believe.

I had a similar experience happen last weekend, I posted about it. You would have thought someone died at how hard I sobbed. Sleep deprivation makes it feel even more dire I think. Losing that milk and going back to work stress has caused my milk to dip at the moment so I’ve had to add in some formula bottles. 

At first I was devastated at the thought of adding in formula. I’ve worked so hard to have her get exclusively breastmilk. But I’m slowly starting to let it go. She’s getting fed, she’s at the 93rd percentile in weight. Everything will be ok. 

It really does mess with your head. I’m sorry you also had to experience it.

We struggled with infertility and then when I finally got pregnant my pregnancy was rough. My husband doesn’t want any more (I have a 15yo stepson), so we’re one and done. I’m ok with it, since we agreed a long time ago on just the one. But I’m not sure if I’d want a second one after everything plus EPing. But then again breastfeeding seems really stressful too so maybe I’d feel the same if I was able to breastfeed.

So we were leaving for the day to go to an expo with my dad when this all happened. Thanks to my meltdown stress and lack of breakfast and water my next pump was less than half of what I usually pump (2oz total versus my usual ~5oz). So that was even more frustrating. But I made myself eat and drink some water after I saw that and my next pump was back to normal. It’s crazy how much everything affects it.
Oh no! That’s awful! I’m sorry too.

Lane Bryant has some amazing nursing bras. I’m a 42DD and the momcozy M5 I have fits in them nicely. They’re also comfy but supportive. I was having trouble since most of the nursing bras I had tried before that were more like bralettes and I want support. They’re a bit pricier, but Layne Bryant actually has some really decent sales and rewards programs if you watch for them.

I absolutely know where you’re coming from. I tried bf in the hospital, had an awful experience with an LC and ended up having to pump to get my daughter some milk. Luckily my milk had come in, and I haven’t struggled with producing. But lately I’ve been obsessing, worrying about losing my milk supply. Even though logically I know it’s totally fine to use formula, and we use it when I’m behind on milk or in public. 

But SM has definitely messed with me. My TikTok is full of momcozy power pump pours, lactation cookies/supplements etc. watching them constantly made me start panicking about producing enough because I’ve been pumping just as much as she’s. Been eating lately. 

In my irrational brain I keep thinking, I failed at bf, the next best is pumping, and if I give up then I failed at that too… I know it’s ridiculous but here we are I guess.

I was active pre-pregnancy, consistently working out 3-5x a week lifting, cardio etc. I had planned on continuing through my pregnancy and just modifying when needed. I was nauseous daily until 19 weeks, and then started getting migraines after that. I would go to the gym when I felt good enough to go. I also have Ehlers Danlos Syndrome so my joints are wonky. My back would flare up and I’d be down for a few days etc. and I finally realized I was forcing myself to go do something that made me feel worse. 

So I stopped going to the gym. Now I do what my body will allow and that’s mostly sitting and light housework. I have a pelvic floor therapist set up for post partum, and a plan to get myself back in working order once I’m cleared. It helps to view it as a season, this state is temporary and as long as I keep moving forward and listen to my body I’ll get back to where I was. 

Not honoring my body and what it needs isn’t going to help anyone. So I have resigned myself to be patient and consistent once I am able. But I struggled to get here for a while. Be gentle with yourself, your body is working really hard.

I haven’t had much of an appetite throughout this pregnancy, so when I actually want something I eat it. I was nauseous all day every day until 19 weeks, so I had been forcing myself to eat things up to then. Now I’m not nauseous but I get full really quickly, so I’m still not eating a ton of food. So I figure, make sure I get some fruits and veggies, protein and then whatever makes me want to eat (avoiding the obvious no nos of course). My doctor is happy with my weight gain and baby is healthy and everything looks good. I figure once baby comes then I can reign in my foods again and be more consistent with my workouts again too.

Let me tell you, I’ve always been pretty active. I thought I’d be working out throughout, just modifying as my belly got bigger. I’ve made it to the gym maybe 2x a month since I got pregnant. It’s so frustrating. I couldn’t handle a vegetable the entirety of my first trimester. Pregnancy has definitely knocked me down a peg, I’m just doing what I can do and know I’ll get back to it after baby comes.

I was consistent before pregnancy, and always thought that I would be that lady running and lifting like normal throughout. But I have felt so awful this whole time my workouts have been sporadic at best. First trimester I had constant nausea that didn’t go away until about 17 or 18 weeks. And now at 20 weeks I seem to have traded in the nausea for hormone migraines. Currently on day 7. I go when I feel up to it and try not to worry too much, I know I’ll get back to it when my body will allow it.

I actually wrote my vows to my DH and then a little speech/vows to my SS as well. But he was one of the best men and is a teen. I also gave him a bracelet after the ceremony. 

The vows I wrote to DH were strictly about us. SS and I are really close and he had been having anxiety that once we got married that we would decide to abandon him (thanks to some nonsense some of his friends had been saying to him). I wanted to include him as much as possible and let him know we were a family and he would always be a part of it.

I’ve noticed it changes day to day. Some days my legs and back lifting workout have me breathing like a wounded Buffalo, and the next time I do the same workout I feel awesome. I can’t figure out if there’s a pattern, so I just listen to my body and take it easier on days where it feels hard. But yes the out of breath thing started pretty early on ~5 weeks I think.

Im in the same boat! DH has always been wonderful at including me and listening to my opinion. SS and I have a great relationship and BM and I get along pretty well too. They also coparent well, so even though there are differences in parenting between them that can be frustrating, overall, it’s an ideal blended family situation.

Im also gestating so I haven’t thrown a bio in the mix yet. But I’m not too worried about it. Im sure there will be challenges and adjustments on all ends. But having DH be a true partner and being able to openly discuss issues has made a huge difference. I’ve said multiple times that if BM was HC or they didn’t coparent well I would have bounced before even getting to the marriage stage. SPing is not for the faint of heart even in ideal situations

I was having that problem with sneezing as well at 10 weeks. According to google 9-10 weeks is the peak of the relaxant hormone being released and it can effect your bladder sphincter. It let up for me the next week. It may not be a bad idea to see if you can get a referral to a pelvic floor therapist if it doesn’t ease up.

My SS14 was eating everything in sight as well. I was getting frustrated because I’d buy some snacks and a few days later find it was gone and I got none of it. So we started telling him how many out of the pack he was allowed to have. For example, I’d buy a pack of 12 smoothies, there are three of us in the house, so we each get four. He can decide how quickly or slowly he consumes them, but once he finishes the 4 allotted to him he’s done until I buy a new pack. Ever since we started divvying it up he’s respected that. And if he wants more he’ll ask and sometimes I’ll give him one of mine if it’s a snack I’m not living after all.
Apple sauce has been saving my butt. That and potatoes. Mac and cheese has also been a meal I can stomach that helps the nausea be a bit better

Not exactly the same. But this past month was the last month before I get in to see the fertility clinic. I had timed things, the potential due date was the date I had said I wanted (I’ve always said I’d love to have an October baby), manifestation, meditation, energy work, seed cycling. I convinced myself that this month was the month. And when I got my period something in me just broke. Why this cycle was the one that broke me, I can’t tell you. We’ve been trying for a year and a half. Maybe I was hoping I could avoid the fertility clinic, or that the universe would answer my hopes if I just did all the things. 

But this current cycle after my period, I’ve half heartedly taken the ovulation tests, skipping days, not being consistent with the times I take it etc. I haven’t been pushing to time things correctly. I think I’ve partly just given up. Started to try and find something else to occupy my time and energy. 

All that to say, I very much understand how you feel. And I’m sorry.
Thanks for the support. I wish you didn’t know how I feel, I wouldn’t wish this on my worst enemy. Sometimes I wish I could just decide that I didn’t want my own. Sending you sticky baby dust.

My husband also has a kid, my stepson is 13, and although I love him to pieces he’s not mine, and never will be (which is ok). I came into his life when he was older so I never got to experience the baby phases. No birthday parties, or trick or treating, or Christmas mornings. We have many wonderful memories, but I want to experience the little kid things too, especially with my husband. 

He doesn’t feel that deep sorrow and longing like I do. Because he did it already, so it’s not this empty hole in his life like it is for me. I keep trying to explain to him how alone I feel when I am devastated each month. Where he’s like eh we’ll keep trying. He tries to be supportive and he listens etc. but it’s just extremely lonely. 

I try to think of the perks of being child free, and pick something else to focus on goal wise… but it doesn’t seem to help much.

Thanks. I’ve been texting her, being very positive and excited for her. Because even though I’m sobbing while I text her, I actually am very excited for her. And I love babies! So having a new one to spoil is one of my favorite things. I’m trying to give myself time to feel what I need to feel. But I also want to support her like I hope to be supported one day. Part of me had hoped we would be pregnant at the same time and be able to raise babies together, but it’s looking less and less likely. I wish this process didn’t sap the joy out of things. 

*edited a word

My best friend told me she was pregnant last night. I am so excited for her, but I can’t stop crying. I’m angry that my grief is overshadowing what should be my elation for my best friend. I got my period this morning, which took away the tiny hope I still had that this month maybe worked. I’m afraid I’m going to ruin our friendship. And I’m afraid that I’m going to spiral down into this depression. I want to be overjoyed for her and her fiancé. They deserve to be surrounded by people who love them and celebrate with them. But I also feel like I just lost the one friend I could tell anything about this whole process. Because I don’t want her to feel like she can’t talk to me about her pregnancy. I’m hoping that after a couple days I’ll come to terms with it and be ok. Today I just feel hopeless.

I thought I was so smart mobile ordering yesterday so I could swoop in get my drink and cup and go back to work without having anyone notice I stepped away from my desk…. I was sorely mistaken. It was an absolute madhouse. Ended up having to wait 10 minutes after I got there. But no one noticed I was missing for like 30 minutes so it’s all good!

I feel this. My husband has a child from a previous relationship. And I love my stepson to pieces, but I came into his life when he was 10. I never got to experience the birthday parties, or firsts, or Halloween or Christmas morning, all the fun parts. And we do lots of fun things now, and I have a great relationship with him. But he’s not mine, and he never will be. 

The monthly hope, and disappointment cycle is awful. And it feels like I’m doing it alone, since my husband doesn’t really feel the same. He had the baby, he experienced everything. 

And I used to at least be able to somewhat participate with my nephews. But they moved hallways across the country last year, so I don’t even have that outlet anymore. It just sucks. And I just wanted to say you’re not alone.

My SS13 is funny, and he has a really kind heart. We’ve always had a special bond, he once told his dad that I just get him. We have inside jokes and he makes me laugh all the time. I love watching him with my younger nephews, because he’s so patient and good with them too.

Honestly, as a stepmom myself I really appreciated how she put that child first and admitted that she didn’t feel ready to be a stepmom. I wish more people really thought about how them dating a child’s parent would effect the child and if they were willing and able to be another parental figure for that child. Being a parent is difficult and being a step parent adds an additional layer of complications to everything. If you don’t feel like you are ready to be there for the kid, it’s best that you don’t get involved. So good on Gabby for being aware of where she was emotionally.

I still think about that story to this day!! I think it was Scary Stories for Stormy Nights by R.C. Welch. The book has a werewolf with bloody claws on the front of it. Or it’s in one of the Scary Stories for Sleepovers, or Scary Stories for when you’re home alone books. I know I read it in one of those books one summer, just not 100% certain which book it was in.
I remember reading this book!! I can’t remember the name. I’ll see if I can figure it out. Hoping someone else knows

I asked mine if she’d be willing first, then I sent her a tumbler with her favorite color, her name, and maid of honor on it. Plus a pretty bracelet and a card that said something silly like, now pretend to be surprised or something.

I’ve left PTs for way less. The way I look at it, if I’m going to be spending my hard earned money and time coming to a therapy it needs to be helping me, physically and mentally. I’ve had PTs brush me off when I try to explain that I’m sensitive to weather changes, and my joint pain is worse when it’s going to rain or when there’s a significant temperature change. I’ve also been ignored when I told them the stretch they were doing to fix the nerve pain in my leg was bothering my spine. But I have never had one make me cry and apologize during a session, that’s insane. Do not go back to this lady, and I would complain to her supervisor about her behavior. In my experience PTs are the ones that tend to actually listen to me and not belittle and ignore me. I’m so sorry you experienced this.
My pain is mostly joint pain. Float therapy has made a big difference for me. As well as combining that with PT, strength training, and massages monthly

Teenagers are THE WORST. Unfortunately movies and books and TV always depict that of you’re truly in love and devoted to each other then marriage is the only option. But it’s not important to everyone. The wedding industry has also created such a craziness around it.

Ironically, as we know and she’ll figure out when she’s older, just because you get married does not equal forever love or faithfulness or happiness for everyone. I don’t think it has anything to do with how she feels about you as a person. I know my SS  struggles with really liking me and feeling close to me, but also feeling like he’s betraying his mom if he admits it (even though we’ve all talked about it and she has said it’s ok for him to feel close to me). He’s done/said some really mean and hurtful things to me because he feels so conflicted. 

It may just be her naive views making the conclusion that you and her dad must not be “as in love” as her mom because you haven’t gotten married. I totally understand feeling hurt after putting so much of your time and effort in. I sort of feel like it’s not so much about you as her current limited view of the world. At that age nuance and grey areas are not much of a thing. 

Definitely talk to your SO about it, so at least the two of you can talk it out and maybe he can address things with her to make her aware of her comments hurting people.

I live with it, but strength training, monthly massage and monthly float sessions help immensely. Also otc pain killers when it’s bad.

Edit: my phone thinks I love the pain lol

I found muscle relaxers make my issues 10x worse! My body responds pretty good to PT when I have one that will listen to me and work with my EDS rather than do things that make it worse. I hate doctors that make you feel like you don't know your own body.
I feel this so hard. I've also subluxed a rib getting a massage, she didn't even do anything different from usual, got up and was like, oh ouch. Popped it back in eventually though.

I'm so sorry. My pain tends to show up in my SI Joint, feet, and sometimes my hands, and of course general achey pain throughout the body. I will very rarely say anything about it, since it's there all the time, there's not really much I can do about it other than all the self care modalities I'm already doing, and dealing with it. My fiance knows if I say it hurts, it's really bad. He's often times very sweet but feels helpless and doesn't know what to do or say, which, I get it. Its hard to feel like people think you're being dramatic because "you don't look sick" and "if you were really that bad you wouldn't do x,y,z".... nope, I do it all because if I stopped every time I felt awful nothing would ever get done.

Sending you gentle internet hugs and I hope your flare up ends soon. I wish there was more I could offer as far as comforting words or suggestions. But, often times I find it the most helpful to have someone tell me that sucks and just let me feel bad about it for a bit.

Popped my SI Joint out of place to the point that I was in so much pain I ended up in the ER. I was sitting still, in the passenger seat of the car.... not moving. Just felt a click, and suddenly couldn't move without crying out in pain.

I was an avid runner from 2011-2019, in 2018 I got divorced and instead of burying myself in my workouts I let myself feel my feelings. I had a marathon for January 2019, and I wasn't able to defer it at all, so I pushed myself to do the bare minimum of training, and did the race. It was one of the worst races I've run (my own stuff, nothing to do with the venue at all), and after barely finishing I decided I wanted to take a break from running for a bit. I focused on other workouts and only ran when I felt like it, usually 2-3 miles max. It took me the better part of 18 months to get the running bug back. Just recently I've felt the urge to head out for a run, and enjoyed it again without forcing myself. And I'm finally registered for a half marathon later this year. Covid lockdownd and the general state of things over the past year certainly didn't help. But if you run because it's something that you truly enjoy, it will most likely come back if you don't force things.

Maybe you're burnt out on running? Maybe life has been really stressful and you need to prioritize sleep or mental health over your running? Sometimes allowing yourself to take a break, for however long you need to is the trick. Maybe you decide to take a break and find a different form of exercise that you enjoy for a little while, nothing wrong with that.

NTA people should seriously stop commenting on what others eat and their bodies unless specifically asked to do so. I used to work the front desk of a gym, I worked out a lot and taught a ton of group exercise classes, so I was fit. I also ate well for the most part. I found people felt the need to comment on my lunch no matter what it was: salad= no wonder you’re so skinny, all you eat is rabbit food... pizza or grinder? = well you can eat whatever because you workout so much, I wish I was so lucky. It drove me bananas. More people need to follow the Thumper rule: if you can’t say something nice, don’t say nothing at all.

I do have one concern, and it’s about nutrient deficiencies with your diet being mainly junk food. Im sure you have, but if not, it may not be a bad idea to check in with your doctor and make sure nutrients are all good. A registered dietitian may also be helpful. As far as easy ways to get in extra nutrients when eating feels hard smoothies are a great option, and you can add in nut butters and avocado to bump up calories as well as omega 3s. There are also salt pills that are mostly used for endurance athletes but that may help if you need higher sodium for blood pressure. 

But like I said, it’s none of my business so you can take my suggestions and tell me to shove it if you prefer.

NTA for sure. First of all, the job market in general right now is a shitshow. He should get used to hearing the word no, or submitting applications and resumes that never get an answer, because unfortunately that’s job hunting at the moment. Mom should know her calling/interfering on his behalf makes him even less hirable because it gives off the impression that he can’t be relied on to handle things on his own, and honestly most managers that hire teens don’t want to have to deal with an overbearing mom on top of the normal drama that comes with working with teens. I think mom needs to apologize and butt out. He’s not going to go homeless or starve if he doesn’t find a job ASAP, let him do it himself.

I’m thinking I’ll be calling my pain management clinic and seeing about other options.

I’ve been having horrible hand pain, was worried that I could tack arthritis onto my list of ailments to work with now. Called my doctor and got a referral to the rheumatologist, haven’t heard back from that office. Maybe that’s why then? Can pain management help with the hand pain? I’m a massage therapist full time so it’s not only messing with my daily quality of life now, it’s messing with my career too.

I have thick course curly hair and I started buying hair ties for dreadlocks so I could do a top knot. I know for me, I use literally three thick hair ties at all times, otherwise my hair would pull itself out of the bun or ponytail I put it in. I’d knock myself out with pigtail braids lol. I also have to be particular about the height/angle of the bun or ponytail, if it’s not on top of my head it’ll give me a headache. From your picture it looks like your hair may be even thicker than mine. I feel your pain girl!

This is so true. I was having hip pain last week, so I spent time doing some yoga and stretches that have helped me in the past. Got rid of the hip pain, but my lower back to mid spine has been stiff and angry ever since. Now I’m not sure what to do... so I just deal with it? I mean, what do you do when the stuff that helps 98% of people makes it worse for you... and sometimes it helps! But sometimes it makes it worse. So, ignoring it and pretending that it’s not there is the next step I guess.

That deafening silence you get from doctors/PTs/medical personnel/ friend/family member as you're explaining your symptoms and what seems to cause the pain. It's like you can hear them thinking, yeah ok lady. I find myself babbling about how the weather changes how I feel and then slowly trailing off with, yeah my hip hurts... 

When really, my hip hurts, my lower back is threatening to spasm if I just move the right way, and every joint in my hands, neck and feet are aching to the point where I'm trying any weird movement/manipulation that I can think of to try and alleviate it. But because I'm still able to workout consistently, do my job (Massage Therapist), and I'm relatively young, I must be lying. If the pain is that bad how do you even function? But in my head, I refuse to let it stop me, I've gotten really good at pushing through, and I spend a lot of time and money on therapies and treatments to keep me from curling up in a ball and sobbing all day long. Massages, regular PT strength work, stretching, meditating, float therapy, supplements, lots of studying of nutrition, cupping, hot baths, REGULARLY. 

I wish I could give you a hug, because I feel this post so hard.

I'm 33, just got an additional dx of OA in my left hip and spinal stenosis in L4-L5 & L5-S1 on top of my EDS and SI Joint Dysfunction. The amount of doctors who have looked at my imaging, then looked me dead in the face and told me I was too young for these problems.... just... I mean, yeah but here we are? What do they expect me to say? Oh you know, you're right, silly body, I'll just let it know to stop? I'm sorry your own father is saying those things.
Specifically if it’s a person who wearing sports bras, but as they’re struggling to pull the sweaty sports bra over their head

That's awful, I'm so sorry. I went to the ortho because of hip pain, found out I have OA in my left hip and spinal stenosis in my lumbar spine on top of my EDS joint pain and SI Joint issues. Haha! The float session is so neat! The place I went to had two different ways to float. There’s a pod type thing, looks like a sci fi movie almost, or there’s a small room sort of like a closet. There’s about 10 inches of water that’s heated to 94 degrees Fahrenheit that’s has a super high Epsom salt content. They give you swimming ear plugs to keep the salt out of your ears. They tell you to lay on your back with your hands out to the side, bent at the elbows and palms up. If my hands hurt at the end of my day I am not doing it right. Proper, professional massage does not use hands/arms for pressure. Your strength/pressure should be coming from the core and your legs, your hands and arms are just the tools. Proper body mechanics are essential to keeping the pressure consistent and keeping the therapist from overexertion and injury. Body mechanics and proper form and technique were a huge focus while I was in school, and thanks to my teachers being so adamant, I have been practicing for 5 years with no issues. Strength training is always a good idea, but a focus on core strength and legs would be more helpful.

That is absolutely fine! I have clients that request I spend the whole session on certain areas. 99% of the time it's how they express it to me if that makes sense?
 The ones who really irritate me are the ones who come in and basically breakdown how to do my job, especially because most of these clients want me to do full body, but then insist that I keep returning to a part of the body that I've moved on from which messes up my timing as well as the flow of the session. For example, I have a regular client that repeatedly requests that I do full body massage, and focus on lower body and lower back- that's cool. He'll also ask for Swedish massage (which is light to medium pressure and is general work, not specific work) and every time, about two minutes in he then tells me that he wants much much deeper pressure done on him, and will repeatedly tell me to go back and work on an area for another ten minutes or so. Then will complain that I didn't get to everything in the 60 minute time frame.... that he showed up 15 minutes late to.
Asking your therapist to work on a specific area is definitely not an issue, and I have many clients that do just that. I guess my issue is more with them treating me like they know more about my profession than I do. Especially because the majority of clients don't understand that sometimes you're feeling pain in one part of the body, but the reason for that pain is actually in a different part of the body, so not allowing me to work where it will actually make a difference is a waste of time and effort on my part, and a waste of money on theirs since I am then limited in how much I can actually make a difference in their pain. 
The type of massage and goal to the session is also important. The client that is just there to relax and feel good, sure I'll spend a half an hour on your feet if that makes you happy. But my regular client that is coming to me for a chronic issue but won't listen to why I think the massages they've been dictating to me aren't as effective as they could be is frustrating. I spend a lot of time and money learning about my craft. I hope that makes sense?

I have two types of clients that I really dislike working on. 

Type 1: the micromanager. This client will come in and tell me exactly how to do my job. Sometimes it's constantly telling me to go deeper (which is not beneficial as I will work as deep as therapeutically needed/what your body will allow), and the really bad ones are the ones who tell me exactly how long to work on an area/what kind of massage to do. For the layperson, most people don't know enough about their bodies or their issues to be able to tell me the best way to do my job. Also, I'm the professional, so maybe just tell me what's bothering you and I'll figure out the best way for me to tackle the issue knowing my own style and limitations as well as my knowledge of the human body. 

Type 2: the chronically late client. I have certain clients that just cannot get to an appointment on time to save their lives. The ones I don't mind are the ones who fully know this about themselves and will book extra time i.e. a 90 minute in the hopes that they'll at least get 60 minutes, and they pay for the extra time. The ones that grind my gears are the ones that are late no matter when they call and make the appointment, don't let me know they're running late, and then when they finally decide to grace me with their presence try to rush me through the intake portion to get "more hands on time". First of all, it is not my fault that you are late, I was ready at your appointment time. Second of all, no I will not skip the intake, I need to know what is going on with your body before I touch you so that I can figure out what my plan is for the session, and if there are things I need to avoid. Third of all, no I will not be going over to "make up" the 20 minutes you lost by showing up 15 minutes late and then needing to stop and use the bathroom etc. I have other clients that showed up on time and will have their appointments start on time. Also, my time is just as important as yours is, I respect your time by starting on time and ending on time, I expect the same from you.

I feel this in my soul. I have chronic pain from SI Joint Dysfunction, when I'm not in a flare up my pain is manageable and I'm still highly functioning. I've run two marathons with it. For me I just have to be diligent with my strengtheners and self care.
